name: Cinematic 7-section emotional arc: open-voiced piano → sustained strings → chord-tone ostinato → motif melody → countermelody climax with doubles → bookend return to opening
goal: Write a short cinematic cue as a clear emotional journey in ~seven 8-bar sections: open-voiced piano (+ low boom / reverse piano / low drone) → extend 8-bar progression with chord-order variation → add sustained strings under piano (keep reverse piano for continuity) → add short/spiccato string ostinatos built only from chord tones with the same shape transposed per chord → write an 8-bar melody from a 2-bar motif (copy rhythm, change notes; put the highest note in the second half) → repeat melody with an independent countermelody in the rests/sustains, then climax by doubling melody in unison + octaves and adding a pulsing bass-synth push → bookend by copying the opening 8 bars after the crescendo. Delta vs emotional-cinematic-arrangement-arc (melody withheld until climax) and three-track-cinematic-sketch: this keeps piano+strings present earlier, uses chord-tone ostinato shape-lock, and closes with a literal bookend of the opening material.

source.title: How to compose Cinematic Music (in 7 easy steps)

prerequisites: Any DAW with piano, sustained strings, short/spiccato strings (or synth equivalents), and a simple bass/synth for pulse
Basic diatonic chord knowledge in one minor (or major) key

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Key for the cue (source example: C minor)

inputs.name: four_chord_palette
inputs.description: Four diatonic chords to rotate (source example: Cm, Ab, Bb, Ab)

constraints: Original composition recipe; not affiliated with sample-library vendors named in the source. Recreate with any piano/strings/synth; do not copy proprietary presets or libraries.
Ostinato notes must stay inside each bar's chord tones (transpose the shape, don't keep absolute pitches).
Countermelody plays mainly where the main melody sustains or rests.
Steady pitch preference; no random pitch wobble.
Drums early if used (Matt): by about count 8; otherwise pad/piano-led intro is fine.

steps.action: List diatonic chords in the key; pick four. Write bars 1–4 as open-voiced piano chords with a delicate feel. Underpin with a low boom, a reverse-piano pattern, and a quiet low drone so texture is already cinematic.
steps.expect: Soft open intro with room to grow

steps.action: Extend to an 8-bar progression by reordering the same four chords for bars 5–8 (slight variation, same palette).
steps.expect: 8-bar harmonic loop with mild second-half change

steps.action: Next ~8 bars: add long sustained strings under the piano. Optionally tweak one chord. Keep the reverse-piano pattern for continuity. Layer two complementary string timbres if available (thick but not muddy).
steps.expect: Warm bed under piano; continuity from intro FX

steps.action: Add movement with short/spiccato (or synth-pluck) ostinatos: copy the prior 8-bar chords; for each bar invent a short pattern using only that chord's tones; when harmony changes, keep the shape/rhythm but retarget pitches to the new chord.

Write the melody starting with the ostinato section: invent a 2-bar motif from chord tones, fill gaps by step; copy the rhythm into the next 2 bars with new notes; reuse that rhythm in the second half of the 8 bars; place the highest note in the second half for an emotional arc. Orchestrate with violins (+ piano double); optional horns/trumpets/cellos.
steps.expect: 8-bar melody with clear contour peak late

steps.action: Repeat the 8-bar melody as climax: add an independent countermelody (e.g. horns) that enters on main-melody sustains/rests. Double the melody in unison (violins+cellos) and in octaves (violins+piano) in the second half; add a pulsing bass-synth on roots for low-end push.
steps.expect: Peak emotional section with denser orchestration

steps.action: Bookend: after the crescendo, paste the opening 8 bars of piano (+ delicate texture) so the piece ends where it began, feeling final rather than abruptly cut.

verification: Section map is audible: delicate piano → strings → ostinato motion → melody → climax doubles → calm bookend.
Ostinato notes are always chord tones for the current bar.
Melody peak (highest note) lands in the second half of its 8 bars.
Countermelody does not fight the main tune on the same strong attacks.
